@graph.headline: Home Builder Lead Generation and Follow-Up
@graph.description: Build a home builder lead generation process that defines fit, assigns follow-up, preserves source data, and turns inquiries into useful sales feedback.

mainEntity.name: What counts as a home builder lead?

acceptedAnswer.text: A home builder lead is a person who raises a hand through a call, form, booking, reply, or another agreed action. It becomes a qualified opportunity only after the sales team accepts it against documented fit criteria.

mainEntity.name: What information should a builder lead form request?

acceptedAnswer.text: Request only the information needed to route and prepare the next conversation, such as contact details, general market, project type, timing, and planning stage. Ask for sensitive or detailed project information later when it is necessary.

mainEntity.name: Should every inquiry go directly to sales?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Sales-ready inquiries, earlier-stage planners, vendors, job applicants, and unrelated requests need different routes. The routing rules should be visible, tested, and owned.

mainEntity.name: How should home builders measure lead quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Track verified stages and reasons: inquiry, contact, acceptance, nurture, disqualification, consultation, and later pipeline outcomes. Keep platform events separate from sales-confirmed outcomes until the data is reconciled.

Acknowledgements, assignment, task creation, reminders, and approved nurture can be automated. A person should still own qualification, exceptions, sensitive questions, and the actual sales conversation.
